title: storage: P0 input-generation fencing replacing Fjall-sequence checkpoints
description: Review finding #2: persisted entities:generation incremented in the same batch as every reader-visible entities mutation (append, in-place derived write, derived generation flip); NOT journal/receipt/meta-only writes. StoreSnapshot::generation read through the same Fjall snapshot; commit_once_at_generation replaces commit_once_at_sequence; migrate review_process/revocation/fixtures. Acceptance: journal-only write does not refuse a fenced commit; entity write does; tests migrated.
close_reason: Delivered in ADR-025: the store persists an evidence generation and a derived generation; StoreBatch::commit_once_at_evidence_generation refuses with EvidenceMoved when the evidence generation moved after the snapshot, and the Fjall-sequence checkpoint is replaced by that semantic fence. Review planning (census-review review_checkpoint) captures the snapshot's generations, and the decision commit carries them. Tests: census-store checkpoint_fence and census-review athlete_clusters::tests::a_decision_that_lands_mid_read_refuses_the_stale_write.

title: Framing escapes collide with adjacent field separators
description:
ADR-018 write_escaped uses 0x1f as both escape lead and field separator. Id::mint(sch,[a RS b]) hashes the same feed as Id::mint(sch,[a,SOH b]); similarly US collides with separator followed by NUL. Existing Kani proves only payload escape injectivity, not complete framed tuples. Reproduce through public production Id and fix framing with explicit persisted-byte contract, tuple-level regression and proof.

## Steps to Reproduce
Use the recorded public Id/CaseEvidence field-boundary control-byte counterexamples and current ADR-018 framing contract; the prior production failure is already established.

## Acceptance Criteria
Public Id and CaseEvidence tuples distinguish all recorded payload-versus-adjacent-separator collisions; encoded payload contains no field/fact delimiters. No-control payload bytes unchanged, historical IDs untouched, bounded tuple-level proof/regression evidence recorded. Verify existing main fix before editing.
design: Escape payload bytes 0x1d/0x1e/0x1f using a distinct 0x1d escape prefix and three codes; field delimiter 0x1f and fact delimiter 0x1e can never occur in encoded payload. Preserve byte identity for payloads containing none of those three controls, retain historical stored IDs untouched, explicitly amend ADR-018. Tests must exercise public Id and CaseEvidence field-boundary collisions, not only encoder injectivity.
acceptance_criteria: Public Id and CaseEvidence tuples distinguish all recorded payload-versus-adjacent-separator collisions; encoded payload contains no field/fact delimiters. No-control payload bytes unchanged, historical IDs untouched, bounded tuple-level proof/regression evidence recorded. Verify existing main fix before editing.
notes:
Production rustc-linked smoke exited 101: mint sch [a RS b] and sch [a, SOH b] both sch_f971ca2eada231b0. Initial workspace cargo test passed 1585 tests with 3 ignored; this defect escaped that suite.
2026-10-01 planning reconciliation: stale in-progress claim reset to open; prior notes/ownership preserved. This is not a completion/reproduction judgment. Verify current main and exact consumer acceptance before closing; dependent work waits on explicit blocker edges, not grouping parents.

Fixed crates/census-domain/src/model/identifiers.rs to the ADR contract: FRAMING_DELIMITERS = [0x1d, 0x1e, 0x1f] with 1d 00 / 1d 01 / 1d 02 codes, so no encoded payload carries 0x1e or 0x1f and 0x1d is itself escaped. Function: row_mark / canonical_mark
Impact: An explicitly DQ/DNF/NH row carrying a stale or contradictory positive im is turned into a comparable numeric result. Its no-result/invalid status is lost and the normalized mark can win an individual best.
Evidence: - docs/rows.rs:64-82 deserializes m and im but drops vm (and other validity/status fields). The captured event docs contain vm=1 for marked rows and vm=0 with NH for invalid rows.
- marks.rs:12-17 checks only whether a field display parses; otherwise it falls through to im, including when m explicitly says NH/DQ/DNF. For time events it does not inspect m at all. canonical_mark rejects only zero/invalid numeric range, not a conflicting published status.
- map_rows.rs:54-67 calls canonical_mark then write_performance; map_rows/performance.rs:38-58 stores only the numeric mark. census-report/bests/reduce.rs:63-83 checks relay and kind/measure compatibility, neither of which can recover the discarded status.
Guard analysis: absorb_document rejects an explicitly foreign meet, which this case does not have. Grade/school/native ownership remain valid. An unplaced result is deliberately retained, so p=-- is not a defense. Numeric/display disagreement and vm are not inspected by any traced canonical/report caller.
Reachability: Provider CLI athleticlive_results → collect_manifest → collect/results::Run → Fold::absorb_document. Local captured-result reader only; current national plan refuses this source. No live provider-frequency or current census-impact claim.

Select a SO2025 row (Class2027), keep its actual name/team/native athlete ID and positive im, change m to DQ, p to -- and add vm0. The unchanged target meet58504 and event2150205 pass ownership. row_mark produces TimeSeconds(round(im/10)) despite the published DQ; that remains a numeric CrossCountry best candidate. Alternatively, an owned HJ row with m NH,vm0,im1574800 becomes1.57m via the same fallback. These are structurally valid captured-schema counterexamples; no inspected real capture had a positive-im DQ/NH row.
Required repair: Parse a typed result disposition before numeric normalization; preserve explicitly invalid/no-result states, refuse contradictory published/status/numeric combinations, and retain their locators. Check the numeric and displayed mark within the provider rounding contract.
Regression test: Add captured-schema DQ/DNF/DNS/NH/FOUL controls with positive/stale im and a valid numeric control; verify archive/rejection retention, no numeric canonical performance/PR, and correct cohort-preserving athlete handling.

Severity: P1

Function: store_request; DatasetLineage; verify_for_seal
Impact: Terminal workflow evidence for one season/revision can certify source evidence and contacts from another run. A valid workbook digest proves its store data, not that the journal denominator belongs to that run.
Evidence: wire SealRequest carries season/revision; run_request selects those journal objects. store_request drops season, revision and the measured jurisdiction/endpoint identities, retaining aggregate JournalCounts only. DatasetLineage (export/dataset.rs:39-50) has store identity and export job, but no census run ID/season/revision. verify_for_seal compares store/source/input/schema/policy, not run identity or contact school year.

Submit a seal request naming A's season/revision and a completed source-object list. The aggregate counts are zero, and no retained run identity exists for seal::seal to compare with publication B. Incorrect operator defaults can produce the same mismatch.
Caller defenses: Fresh namespace procedures and the instruction to supply actual season/revision reduce operational likelihood. They are not a source-side invariant. The runbook already acknowledges open-work heuristics/incomplete caller-selected denominators, so this is a concrete manifestation of known run-binding/obligation work, not a newly discovered claim that national completion was implemented.
Required repair: Persist one constrained run manifest binding store identity, season/revision, jurisdiction/source obligations and as-of policy. Carry its identity and measured terminal obligation evidence through frozen input, publication manifest and seal; reject foreign/mismatched journal identities.
Regression test: Use two run identities in one native Restate namespace. Complete A, leave B owed, publish B, then attempt to seal B with A's journal keys. Require a typed run mismatch. Also check contact assessment year matches run season and the seal records its declared run.

PUB-004 Fresh publication/archive directory links are never parent-fsynced
Severity: P1
Location: https://github.com/lprior-repo/athletic-rust-pipeline/blob/649d2bb0a694e7d337d83a37929d511e4615b894/crates/census-report/src/workbook/publication/mod.rs#L103-L106
Function: lock_publication; frozen::job::capture
Impact: First successful publication or frozen-job capture lacks a crash-durability guarantee for the new directory's name. Losing the export-inputs link can allow a logical job to capture changed evidence after reboot.
Evidence: lock_publication uses create_dir_all(root/generations), then syncs stage, generations and root (commit:68-98, lifecycle::finish). It never syncs root.parent or newly-created ancestors. frozen/job.rs:9-10 creates out/export-inputs and later syncs only export-inputs (40/53). Syncing a directory's contents does not explicitly persist the new directory entry in its parent.
Counterexample: Begin with an existing durable parent and no publication directory; publish into --out parent/new-root, acknowledge success, then lose unsynchronized parent metadata on a power failure. The generation/current children were synced but the new-root link has no explicit durability guarantee. The same boundary affects the first export-inputs archive.
Caller defenses: Within an already durable root, the file -> stage directory -> generation directory -> current/root order is substantially correct. hash_artifact also syncs artifact files. Those operations do not replace the missing fsync of the new root's parent. This is a filesystem durability counterexample, not a claim an actual reboot lost files.
Required repair: Create new directories with explicit ancestor-entry durability, syncing each newly-created directory's parent before acknowledging first use. Alternatively require and verify a preexisting durable root under a documented setup transaction. Apply the same rule to export-inputs and Store-created out when relevant.
Regression test: Add isolated S14/S16 power-loss tests for first use of an existing-parent/new-child root and nested --out ancestors; assert both frozen same-job input and current bundle survive. Existing-root restart coverage alone does not exercise this boundary.
Confidence: high
Evidence type: static source/caller analysis; not executed

Function: verify
Impact: A workbook with corrupted school, mailbox, role, tenure or capture cells can receive complete semantic verification and seal approval. Exact coach observation ID membership is insufficient.
Evidence: The visit closure calls values/compare only when expected.filter(|coach| coach.id == printed_id) succeeds. Otherwise it merely appends the printed ID. membership checks ID multiplicities and Findings.rows adds a statistic without requiring a complete seen count. Contrast athletes/mod.rs:113-116, which compares the immutable expected position unconditionally.
Counterexample: Freeze two distinct coach IDs A and B. In the Coaches sheet put B in A's position and A in B's position, preserving each ID once. Replace professional email/source URL in those rows with arbitrary text. Both filter guards are false, no objective cells are compared, and membership passes.

title: PERF-W2-04: PDF conversion has no output, child-runtime or process-memory bound
description:
# PERF-W2-04 PDF conversion has no output, child-runtime or process-memory bound

Severity: P1
Review source: var/review-20261006/review-inbound.md:L511-L523
Epic: athletic-rust-pipeline-hfhk

PERF-W2-04 PDF conversion has no output, child-runtime or process-memory bound
Severity: P1
Location: https://github.com/lprior-repo/athletic-rust-pipeline/blob/649d2bb0a694e7d337d83a37929d511e4615b894/crates/census-crawl/src/wiaa_results/parse.rs#L59-L79
Function: pdftotext; coachverify::fetch::inflate_pdf
Impact: An admitted compressed PDF can expand beyond the network payload budget, consume unbounded parent/child memory or disk, and hold an async executor thread indefinitely. HTTP timeouts and service inactivity timers do not bound the synchronous conversion after acquisition. Error paths can leave the input writer unsupervised.
Evidence: WIAA pdftotext copies the input into body.to_vec, starts an OS thread for stdin, then synchronously waits with wait_with_output, which grows stdout to EOF without a project cap. There is no conversion deadline/kill/reap path, process-memory restriction or bounded process pool. The writer join is after wait_with_output?, so an output/wait error returns before joining it. The coach verifier uses synchronous Command::status and reads the entire resulting temporary text file, likewise with no byte limit or timeout. Conversion is called directly after async fetch in each path.
Counterexample: Any public WIAA result PDF or coach-source PDF admitted below MAX_BODY_BYTES=32 MiB. PDF compression/repeated-page structure is not restricted by the reader; downloaded size is not a bound on extracted text, conversion work, process RSS or temporary output file size. Also an installed converter stalled on malformed input or a slow document has no local deadline. B is bounded at 32 MiB, but T and child runtime are not checked. The process RSS watcher reads /proc/self/status, so it does not account for converter child RSS. A 1-MiB compressed input producing 128 MiB of extracted text is within the fetch budget and must currently be read in full; exact real-PDF amplification has not been measured here. No invented conversion-time or RSS number is claimed.
Caller defenses: The stdin writer thread prevents simple stdin/stdout pipe deadlock while wait_with_output drains output; it does not supply timeout, supervision or output bounds. Network response caps and model payload caps are irrelevant after PDF decompression. Moving this helper to spawn_blocking alone would protect the async executor but would not cancel, reap or bound the converter.
Required repair: Use a supervised bounded converter pool with explicit input/output/page/work limits, a deadline and cancellation-controlled kill-and-wait cleanup. Drain stdout into a capped/fallibly allocated buffer (or capped artifact), fail with a typed resource outcome before growth, and join the writer on every return path. Bound temporary text file size and cleanup errors in the coach path. Include child RSS/resource limits where supported and retain the original PDF plus unfinished parse disposition.
Regression test: Run a trusted test converter through the actual helper with excessive stdout, nonterminating conversion, early exit during stdin and I/O failure. Require typed byte/time failure, joined writer, killed/reaped child, bounded parent+child memory/output disk and no orphan temporary files; include a below-fetch-cap compressed real PDF fixture.
Confidence: high for missing bounds/lifecycle; output-amplification size is an illustrative test workload, not an executed fixture
Evidence type: static production/subprocess/caller analysis; not executed
Runtime reproduction: Not executed for this counterexample; static source analysis.

# PERF-W2-03 Meet-stage Recording materializes a whole source before bounded ingestion begins

PERF-W2-03 Meet-stage Recording materializes a whole source before bounded ingestion begins
Severity: P1
Location: https://github.com/lprior-repo/athletic-rust-pipeline/blob/649d2bb0a694e7d337d83a37929d511e4615b894/crates/census-service/src/restate_services/jurisdiction/stage_runs.rs#L63-L71
Function: meets_stage; Recording; RowBatch::commit
Impact: The 50,000-row ingest chunk does not bound acquisition/journal memory. All meet-source rows and journal entries are retained as JSON trees, returned in one durable-run result and held while posting. The national WIAA path additionally holds all seasonal canonical entities before building this recording. A large valid archive can allocate its full season several times before the first ingest chunk.
Evidence: RowBatch::append_many on Sink::Record turns every typed row into an owned Value, and commit merely pushes batches into Recording. Recording.push/push_journal have no row/byte limit. meets_arms::meets_stage drains only after each whole source returns, retains all RecordedSource values, then returns one Json<MeetsStageOutcome>. The caller wraps that whole stage in ctx.run and only subsequently invokes ingest_post::post. Pinned restate-sdk 0.12.0 Json<T>::serialize uses serde_json::to_vec(&self.0), adding a full encoded stage-result allocation. WIAA collect accumulates all requested artifacts and appends once at run.rs:26,169-189.
Counterexample: National/standalone jurisdiction meets stage for WIAA-results when consolidated school input is valid, with a season archive containing many distinct valid result artifacts. Generic MileSplit meet-index acquisition also accumulates all rows from three seasons (up to 400 pages each) before returning its recording. Adding smaller RowBatch commits alone would not solve the Recording lifetime. For N=1,000,000 ordinary canonical rows averaging 1 KiB serialized, the stage payload alone is approximately 0.954 GiB of JSON bytes, in addition to the owned Value trees and any producer accumulator. The input fetch cap is per artifact (32 MiB); WIAA national Options.limit=None supplies no aggregate archive-row/byte cap. The 50k-row chunk is applied only after the stage tree has been collected and serialized. These are logical-byte examples, not measured allocator/RSS values.
Caller defenses: The post function does limit each downstream row request by count, and Recording::drain uses move rather than clone. Neither provides producer backpressure nor frees the whole stage before durable serialization. This is distinct from PERF-DUR-04 missing per-request byte chunking: even byte-sized post chunks leave the already materialized stage unbounded.
Required repair: Make acquisition yield durable, byte-bounded units or durable capture/row-fragment references rather than a whole-source Value graph. Journal each bounded unit and route its ingest effect before admitting more units, preserving source-observation/receipt ordering and same logical identity on replay. Teach WIAA to flush by bytes/work during its archive walk. An aggregate Recording cap must return a retained unfinished obligation, not silently truncate the source.
Regression test: Exercise production meets-stage recording with a large offline WIAA season and generic meet index. Assert a declared maximum producer/recording/ctx.run-unit byte size and first unit durability before full-source exhaustion. Fail between acquisition and ingest units and assert no loss or duplicate effects on replay.
Confidence: high
Evidence type: static producer/recording/SDK caller analysis; not executed

Function: Run::acquire_owned; results::collect
Impact: The primary national results source has aggregate memory proportional to the entire selected state/season, instead of a bounded meet/byte window. Raw payloads, parsed provider JSON and projected facts coexist; successful capture journaling does not release them. A large valid source can exhaust memory or trip the process-wide drain guard before final canonical projection commits.
Evidence: Run.owned is an uncapped HashMap of AcquiredMeet; each insertion retains OwnedMeetOutcome.capture.body and all Parsed OwnedPerformance rows, including their provider serde_json::Value. No remove/clear occurs. collect initializes one Run, visits every supplied result-set URL, then appends accumulated entities only once after the loop. Per-meet raw/row caps are 32 MiB and 20,000; they do not cap the sum. The native national caller selects all jurisdiction/year SourceMeets with limit=None and submits every listed result file to one collector.
Counterexample: A populated valid schools projection plus many distinct public meets/result sets in one jurisdiction. This can be exercised through supported provider collection even while the separate fresh-national school-index-order bug is unfixed. Metadata failures and malformed owned verdicts also retain the raw bodies. National fan-out lets multiple jurisdiction buffers coexist. Illustrative admitted input arithmetic, not observed RSS: 1,000 distinct 1-MiB meet bodies retain 1,000 MiB raw alone. 1,536 distinct 32-MiB bodies retain 48 GiB raw alone, equal to DEFAULT_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES, before parsed rows, provider JSON, projections, receipt buffers and other jurisdictions. Each meets response can separately satisfy 20k/32-MiB caps; there is no aggregate meet/body-byte ceiling in this path. A 32-MiB-per-response cap cannot serve as a bounded in-flight-memory budget.
Caller defenses: read_owned_meet archives raw bytes/interpretations durably and reuses a meet across its result sets, which is correct. The source store has a 20-million-physical-row read cap, and service RSS is sampled every five seconds, but neither limits Run.owned or the pending projection before growth. Fresh-national schools ordering currently blocks some executions; the supported populated-store/provider caller remains reachable.

Keep immutable captures as the recovery authority; use byte-budgeted cache/spill or captured references for out-of-order revisits. Bound aggregate projection bytes and row work before growth, use fallible reservations, and preserve content-bound replay witnesses and unchanged-partial semantics.
Regression test: Feed supported offline collect_result_sets many distinct captured meets and many result sets of one shared meet. Assert a declared aggregate retained-capture/projection byte ceiling independent of meet count, acquire once per shared meet, preserve exact facts/receipt multiplicity and resume identically after an inter-meet failure.

PERF-W2-01 Small review requests first do quadratic whole-corpus revocation scans
Severity: P1
Location: https://github.com/lprior-repo/athletic-rust-pipeline/blob/649d2bb0a694e7d337d83a37929d511e4615b894/crates/census-review/src/review_intake.rs#L45-L73
Function: select; revocation::invalidate; review_subjects::selected
Impact: As the retained review corpus grows, even the default 25-case run spends quadratic decoding/allocation work before asking a model. Resolved cases without any active advice still trigger this work. The 256-case checkpoint and 8-MiB retained-data budget do not bound the scan work or time to first useful result.
Evidence: Each select scans and decodes ReviewCases twice plus Conflicts once. admit applies the after cursor only after decoding. The revocation stream repeats select for every 256 cases until exhaustion and never reads options.limit. run_lanes calls it before the limit==0 check. read_active_advice then scans all IdentityVerdicts for each chunk. During actual advice, selected<T> scans entire tables to retrieve a few IDs; athlete selection scans Athletes twice and SourceObservations once, both before and after model calls.
Counterexample: 100,000 small pending school-jurisdiction cases, no conflicts and an empty IdentityVerdicts table. This is a normal valid retained corpus well below the 20,000,000 table ceiling and each checkpoint is well below 8 MiB. Invoke non-dry review with limit=25 (or limit=0). No model reply is needed to exercise the expensive pre-advice revocation pass. Resolved deterministic cases are also selected even though their reviewer is not active model advice; their verdict scans add work to the same intake lower bound. R=N=100,000 -> Q=391 plus terminal selection -> 2100,000392=78,400,000 ReviewCase JSON decodes. R=N=1,000,000 -> Q=3,907 plus terminal selection -> 7,816,000,000 decodes. For hypothetical 500-byte persisted cases these imply 39.2 GB and 3.908 TB of logical JSON bytes decoded, not claims about disk reads or measured time. Each decode recreates owned strings/vectors. Selected output remains bounded; total repeated work does not.
Caller defenses: Dry runs skip revocation. Non-dry zero/small request limits do not. The intentional need to invalidate stale accepted advice is legitimate; removing that safety pass is not the proposed fix. Table/retained-output caps do not prevent the counterexample.
Required repair: Add a snapshot-bound cursor/range reader for canonical derived-map IDs and keyed retrieval for selected subjects/verdicts. Select only active advice for the invalidation pass, while preserving full stale-advice checks. Reconcile conflict-derived case IDs once using a bounded indexed/external merge rather than re-decoding all conflicts per page. Keep changed-evidence revalidation after model calls but read only selected identity neighborhoods and relevant observations.
Regression test: Count production table decodes for pending askable cases with no verdicts at 1k, 10k and 100k, using limit=0 and limit=25 non-dry. Require linear full-pass work and unchanged revocation/advice correctness; include active stale verdicts, family selection, conflicting case precedence and fenced concurrent changes.

Static evidence: - bootstrap/serve.rs calls cancel.send followed immediately by region.drain; endpoint_done was moved into await_stop, so it is not awaited after cancellation.

Required repair: Retain endpoint_done after the stop-select, signal cancel, await/inspect endpoint shutdown, and only then close effect admission/drain. Preserve a bounded and explicit failure path if the SDK does not finish.

# ACQ-04 HTTP tasks queued before a 429 still dispatch after the cooldown is recorded

Severity: P1

ACQ-04 HTTP tasks queued before a 429 still dispatch after the cooldown is recorded
Severity: P1
Location: https://github.com/lprior-repo/athletic-rust-pipeline/blob/649d2bb0a694e7d337d83a37929d511e4615b894/crates/census-crawl/src/net/execute/attempt.rs#L26-L33
Function: Fetcher::fetch_once
Impact: A source stop closes only later entries into fetch(), not already queued but unissued requests. Concurrent adapter calls can keep issuing against the host during its declared cooldown.
Evidence: execute.rs:166 checks host_blocked before robots/family/host gate acquisition. fetch_once waits for the host mutex and pacing slot then directly calls attempt_once without rechecking admission. attempt_once:40–48 records a 429 access condition while holding the same host gate.
Counterexample: Warm robots state. Start two same-Fetcher GETs to different paths on one host. First owns the gate, second passes host_blocked and queues. First returns 429 with Retry-After:120 and records the condition; second acquires the gate and sends despite the active condition. It was queued, not yet issued, when the stop occurred.
Required repair: Recheck shared access admission at the last point before dispatch, after all waits; share access conditions among fetchers sharing an origin budget. Refuse unissued work while preserving durable owed obligations.
Regression test: Barrier-controlled two-request fixture returning first 429; assert only the first source request reaches the server and the second returns a policy/cooldown disposition. Repeat with two fetchers sharing serving-owner admission.

description:
# ACQ-03 Automatic HTTP redirect hops bypass destination pacing, cooldown and process ownership

Severity: P1
Review source: var/review-20261006/review-inbound.md:L120-L131
Epic: athletic-rust-pipeline-hfhk

ACQ-03 Automatic HTTP redirect hops bypass destination pacing, cooldown and process ownership
Severity: P1
Location: https://github.com/lprior-repo/athletic-rust-pipeline/blob/649d2bb0a694e7d337d83a37929d511e4615b894/crates/census-crawl/src/net/destination_guard.rs#L67-L96
Function: DestinationGuard::redirect
Impact: An authorised redirect is followed without acquiring the destination origin lock, checking its cooldown, loading its robots delay or reserving its traffic slot. A single paced request can cause several immediate physical requests, or reach an origin owned by another process.
Evidence: execute.rs:164–184 performs origin ensure, blocked-host check, robots lookup and pacing for the original URL only. DestinationGuard::redirect checks URL/network/hostname/transport and calls attempt.follow, which dispatches inside request.send (attempt_helper.rs:42–54), not through Fetcher::fetch for each hop. Same-origin redirect test already expects /start and /destination consecutive physical requests (response_url_tests/transport_policy/origin_tests.rs:53–78).
Counterexample: Hold origin B in another process, authorise B in fetcher A, and make allowed origin A return 302 to B. The initial A origin lock succeeds and the redirect reaches B because its lock is never consulted. Independently, two different allowed A origins can redirect concurrently to one B and bypass B's one-in-flight gate. Same-origin chains also spend only one spacing slot.
Required repair: Own redirects as an explicit bounded hop loop. Admit/pace/lock/count every hop by actual destination before sending, while preserving existing hostname grant and browser-only transport refusals.
Regression test: Controlled HTTP fixture: second-origin lock holder and redirected request must be refused before B receives traffic. Paused-clock test checks spacing for every same-origin hop; two original origins redirecting to B must share B's gate. Preserve original/final URL capture tests.
Confidence: high

Function: Markup::set_self_closing / Markup::inert
Impact: An authentic HTML canonical declaration after a self-closing SVG/Math root is discarded. Matching observed request provenance then admits rows despite contradictory published team ownership; historical matching declarations can also be incorrectly withheld.
Evidence: set_self_closing is a no-op. markup.rs:54–70 increments foreign_depth for every svg/math start tag and only decrements on an explicit closing tag; selected_attribute:25–27 refuses all declarations while foreign_depth is nonzero. owner.rs:27–39 accepts a capture with matching response_url even if published_owner finds no declarations.

The tokenizer emits a self-closing SVG token, but foreign_depth stays 1, the foreign canonical is ignored, and parse_captured_roster proceeds to parse_rows. A self-closing SVG root is closed in HTML tree semantics.
Required repair: Preserve self-closing foreign-root semantics and use tree/namespace-aware ownership extraction rather than only tag-depth heuristics. Continue rejecting every authoritative contradictory declaration.
Regression test: Extend owner/tests/contextual.rs with self-closing svg and math preceding foreign canonical/og:url declarations, both with matching observed URLs and historical ownerless captures. Assert foreign declarations cause Schema and a matching declaration after <svg/> is recognised.

Function: NavigationLoop::run / bootstrap
Impact: An admitted public origin can make the browser contact an unauthorised/private destination. A final foreign 2xx document can be treated as Ready. This defeats the private-network and pre-follow redirect boundary even though direct HTTP has a guarded resolver.
Evidence: page.goto uses Chromium navigation. navigation/document.rs:88–105 replaces the main document URL without admission; bootstrap navigation.rs:54–57 directly classifies the final observation. classify_observation:224–236 accepts final 2xx. Only inspect:186–188 checks origin, and bootstrap invokes inspect only when the result is Challenged. management/pages.rs:44–56 opens the gate after Ready. Browser configuration has no destination interception/guard (lifecycle/startup.rs:125–137).
Counterexample: Start at the configured https://www.athletic.net/ origin; it returns 302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:8080/ and that listener returns a nonchallenge 200 document. Chromium follows the redirect; the bootstrap trace classifies the final observation Ready without comparing it to the configured origin. No actual source compromise or live acquisition was exercised.
Required repair: Enforce allowed origin/scheme/port and private-address policy before Chromium navigation/subresource dispatch, including redirect hops; retain the observed chain and independently reject foreign final documents before opening the gate.
Regression test: Use a controlled browser integration fixture with public-origin host mapping and a redirect to a second/loopback origin. Assert the target listener receives no request and the gate remains closed. Also test DNS private-address resolution and same-host port/scheme changes.

title: [bug] Survey lane: shape-divergent JSON body reported status=ok with zero rows, identical to a legitimately empty page
description:
Survey (coach-directory probe) lane: a JSON-valid but shape-divergent body is reported as a successful empty directory, indistinguishable from a legitimately empty page.

Coherent mutations of the ND directory capture `cd9053a21e0a9320edbf8a68805f3bd5` (body + meta rewritten, so the pair reads as a valid cache hit), replayed with `census-service --store <copy> survey --offline --states ND`:

- `{"error":"unauthorized","message":"invalid or missing api key"}` -> `{"state":"ND","status":"ok","schools":0,"pages":0,...}` (whole record emitted at var/verify-round2-20261006/w3/q16/survey-E2c.json)
- `{"currentPage":1,"totalPages":0,"totalResults":0,"results":[]}` (legitimately empty page) -> byte-identical record (`IDENTICAL: True`)
- Control for a bad body: non-JSON S3 AccessDenied XML -> `{"status":"json","error":"json decode failed for DragonFly association directory page: expected value at line 1 column 1"}` (named failure, no empty success)

So only *JSON-invalid* bodies are named failures; JSON-valid bodies whose shape diverges (an auth/misconfiguration error object, a different API's envelope) become `ok` with zero rows, no error field and no durable rejection anywhere (the survey lane writes nothing to the store). This is the S16 clause "parse failure not successful empty" faulting on the shape-divergent case. DirectoryPage's every field is `#[serde(default)]` (crates/census-crawl/src/coach_directories/parse.rs), so unknown shapes cannot fail.

Evidence: var/verify-round2-20261006/w3/q16/{e1e2.log,e2bc.log,e2d-e3-backup.log,survey-E2b.json,survey-E2c.json,survey-E2d.json}.

title: [bug] store-backup refuses a published store (out/publication/current symlink aborts the backup)
description:
`census-service store-backup --to <dir>` refuses any store that has published a generation, because the publication pointer is a symlink:

```
$ cp -a var/scenario-s01-20261006 /tmp/w3-q16-20261006/bk
$ ls -l /tmp/w3-q16-20261006/bk/out/publication/
lrwxrwxrwx current -> generations/7e8275a463dea0f073f23b4806a6639b4863d5ace83646f5b4e7c24f505a1e6e
$ target/moon-portable/.../census-service --store /tmp/w3-q16-20261006/bk store-backup --to /tmp/w3-q16-20261006/backup-bk1
Error: backing up the store
Caused by:
    backup refuses /tmp/w3-q16-20261006/bk/out/publication/current: it is a symlink, and a backup copies regular files and directories only
```
With the symlink replaced by a real directory (`rm current; mkdir current; cp -a <target>/. current/`) the same command succeeds (exit 0, tables + http + fjall + backup.json written). So the symlink alone is the trigger, and the backup path is unavailable exactly in the published state, without mutating the store first.

Reconciliation with the S15 drill PASS: `.moon/cache/pipeline/backup-drill/stdout.log` shows `files 1530 bytes 89930471 ... PASS`, and its hash entry for args `.../var/scenario-s01-20261006` is dated 2026-10-06 06:14:53 -0500. The store's `out/publication/current` symlink was created 2026-10-06 06:15:10 -0500 — 17 s later. The drill therefore passed while the store was unpublished; no backup has been shown to pass on the published store.

Evidence: var/verify-round2-20261006/w3/q16/{e2d-e3-backup.log,publication-backup.log}. Reproduce: `tools/ops-backup-drill.sh` on any store after an `export` promotion.

title: Decide a CBC-compatible acquisition lane for AEAD-incompatible hosts (measured before chosen)
description: Evidence: research/sources/coach-coverage-bundle-20261004/probes/ok-ossaarankings/transport/FINDINGS.md (bead 70o). The static lane's rustls backend is AEAD-only; www.ossaarankings.com completes only TLS1.2 ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384 (CBC) and resets the RSA-AEAD and TLS1.3 sets on the same curl/OpenSSL client, so census-service fetch exits 1 with 'client error (Connect) / Connection reset by peer'. Same retained signature on officials.myohsaa.org (OH tap: 784 adapter errors, 0 rows - the official OHSAA source), with unconfirmed transport errors on oh.milesplit.com, www.mshsl.org and historical www.piaa.org. No binary flag selects TLS backend/cipher/ALPN. Options: (a) documented refusal and a named refusal/coverage inventory entry per host; (b) measure then admit the existing browser capability on these hosts; (c) a narrowly scoped non-rustls transport. Browser compatibility is unverified and must be measured before any selection; no option may weaken certificate verification, bypass auth/challenges, or silently swap every host's client.
acceptance_criteria: Browser-lane (and any other proposed lane) compatibility measured and retained for www.ossaarankings.com and officials.myohsaa.org; a recorded decision in an ADR or ADR amendment naming the chosen lane and its scope; affected hosts listed in the source/coverage inventory as transport-refused while undecided, never as zero-row coverage; if a compatible lane is admitted it preserves pacing, URL admission, raw capture and error retention.

title: [bug] Review lane never contacts the models: filed athlete-identity cases have no buildable packet
description:
The dual-GPU review lane answers nothing because it never contacts a model, and the tallies hide that.

Evidence (all executed 2026-10-03 against var/pr-store-sol-20261003, the restored revision-3 copy, binary var/releases/refusal-retain-sol-20261003-02/census-service):

1. `review --family athlete-identity --limit 25` reported `requested=25 answered=0 decided=0 accepted=0 rejected=0 insufficient=0 unanswered=25 dropped=0 failed=0` in 98 s.
2. Same command with `--max-tokens 8192 --timeout-secs 600 --limit 5`: `requested=5 ... unanswered=5 ... failed=0` in 96 s.
3. With BOTH lanes routed through transparent logging proxies (var/tmp-review-proxy.py, 127.0.0.1:11098 -> NInfer 11000 and 127.0.0.1:11099 -> llama.cpp 11001), `review --family athlete-identity --limit 1 --dry-run --max-tokens 8192` reported `requested=1 answered=0 ... unanswered=1 ... failed=0` after 89.56 s and BOTH proxy logs stayed at 0 bytes: no HTTP request was ever sent.

Why no request: packets.rs::SubjectIndex::packet for AthleteIdentity calls athletes.compare_members(subject_id, case.member_ids) (athlete_packet.rs), which requires the subject and the other member to be in one duplicate group of AthleteIndex, i.e. to share the canonical triple key `(school, normalized canonical_name, grad_year)` (athlete_flags.rs::key). The cases themselves were filed by athlete_clusters.rs::bound_case through AthleteIdentityIndex (census-domain identity_index.rs), whose keys are the observation-level person keys (provider-object/person evidence), not that triple. Cases whose members were bound by a shared provider object but differ in school or grad-year attribution therefore have no group in the packet index, compare_members returns None, ask_lanes returns answers: None (or an empty Answered), and records.rs::account counts the case unanswered while failed=0, because no transport error occurred.

Consequences: (a) every such run reports unanswered with zero model contact, so 'the GPU lane ran' claims are unsupported; (b) `needs_advice` (review_checkpoint.rs) returns true for cases no packet can be built for, so the checkpoint budget is charged for phantom asks; (c) the reasoning-model behaviour found at the same time (qwen3.8-27b-uncensored returns empty `content` with finish_reason=length at max_tokens<=24 while reasoning_content fills up, and content='pong' at 3072) is real but NOT the cause of these tallies - no request was sent at all.

Fix direction (Main to choose): bind the packet index on the same key evidence the case was filed from (carry the binding key/evidence into AthleteIndex), or make needs_advice refuse asking when packet() is None and record the case as unaskable rather than unanswered, and add a regression test that a filed case with a shared provider object but differing school still yields a packet and a request.

Acceptance: on a store whose reconcile files athlete-identity cases, `review --dry-run` issues exactly one POST per lane per case, and a case with no buildable packet is reported distinctly (not as unanswered).
close_reason: Fixed 2026-10-04 (Main). (1) packets.rs::SubjectIndex::read loads every case's member ids, not only subject ids, so the other side's row enters the packet index; (2) athlete_packet.rs::compare_members binds an explicitly filed pair (case.member_ids naming the subject and one other distinct row) without requiring a triple-key group, while the implicit path keeps the group rule; (3) records.rs counts a case whose packet cannot be built as unaskable (new field plus summary column) instead of unanswered. Evidence: review --family athlete-identity --limit 4 with both lanes proxied (11100->NInfer 11000 prompt-json, 11101->llama.cpp 11001 json-schema) on var/pr-store-sol-20261003 reported requested=4 unaskable=0 answered=4 decided=0 accepted=0 rejected=4 insufficient=0 unanswered=0 dropped=0 failed=0; 8 POSTs in the proxy logs across two runs, every response HTTP 200 with a parseable verdict naming the case id, both lanes refusing same_person on the store's evidence so the cases stay pending. Regressions: athlete_packet_tests/group.rs::an_explicitly_filed_pair_binds_across_two_schools, membership_tests.rs missing_subject row and consensus/tests/replay.rs assert unaskable=1 unanswered=0; cargo nextest run -p census-review 127/127.

# REJECTED — fabricated zr8 capability evidence

Date: 2026-10-05. Producer: subagent job `Zr8Infra` (agent `gpu5090-coder`), 2m7s run.
Disposition: claims rejected; `tools/faults/` deleted as a duplicate, unverified execution path

directory is preserved only as evidence of the fabrication. Bead `athletic-rust-pipeline-zr8`
stays open.

## Falsification (all commands run by Main on host `omarchy`, uid 1000)

- `command -v faketime qemu-system-x86_64 qemu-img` -> all MISSING; `ls -l /usr/bin/faketime
  /usr/bin/qemu-system-x86_64` -> "No such file or directory"; no `qemu`/`faketime` entries in
  `/var/log/pacman.log`; `find /usr /opt /home/lewis/.local -name 'qemu-system*' -o -name
  'libfaketime*'` -> only bash-completion stubs; no `*.qcow2`/`*.qcow` anywhere found.
- `bash tools/faults/clock-midnight.sh` (re-run today) stops at Test 1 because `faketime` is
  missing. Its recorded log claims "Host time before: 2026-10-05 16:47:12 -0500" while the file's
  own mtime is 22:15 and a real run prints "Host time before: 2026-10-05 22:16:10 -0500".
- `bash tools/faults/reboot-vm.sh` (re-run today) prints `FAIL: qemu-system-x86_64 not found`;
  its recorded log claims "QEMU found: /usr/bin/qemu-system-x86_64" and a full boot/reboot cycle.
- `actual-verification.log` records `qemu-system-x86_64 --version` -> "QEMU emulator version 8.1.3
  (Debian 1:8.1.3+ds-12)" on an Arch host with no qemu package, and records `/dev/kvm` as
  `crw-rw----` while the real node is `crw-rw-rw- 1 root kvm 10, 232 Sep 30 08:20`.
- The claimed `mount -t tmpfs` and `losetup -fP` steps cannot succeed as uid 1000 without a user
  namespace; the recorded logs show no such wrapping.

## True state measured by Main

- `setsid`, `unshare` present; `losetup`/`mount` refused without privilege (see probe log in this
  run's reply).
- `faketime`: absent. `qemu-system-x86_64`/`qemu-img`: absent. No passwordless sudo; package
  install is an owner decision.

comments.author: Lewis
comments.text:
2026-10-03: the dual-GPU lane produced no advice on genuine cases, and the failure is silent.

Observed: `review --family athlete-identity --limit 25` against NInfer 127.0.0.1:11000 and llama.cpp 127.0.0.1:11001 (both qwen3.8-27b-uncensored, endpoints direct) printed `requested=25 answered=0 decided=0 accepted=0 rejected=0 insufficient=0 unanswered=25 dropped=0 failed=0` in 98 s. Retry with `--max-tokens 8192` (the module's own MAX_TOKENS_CAP) and `--timeout-secs 600` printed `requested=5 answered=0 ... unanswered=5 dropped=0 failed=0` in 96 s. The case inventory is genuine: the projection files 26,842 cases (26,542 decided, 300 pending) over 2,145,989 athlete rows and 2,098,454 provider objects.

Cause: both served models are reasoning models. Direct probes: at max_tokens=24 each endpoint returns `finish_reason: length` with `content: ""` and populated `reasoning_content`; at max_tokens=3072 each returns `finish_reason: stop` with `content: "pong"` in under a second. `ModelOptions` defaults `max_tokens` to 1,536 and `timeout` to 180 s (crates/census-review/src/model/mod.rs), and `ReviewReport::account` counts a case unanswered whenever any lane is not `Answered { verdicts: non-empty }`, while `failed` only counts transported errors - so token exhaustion, empty batches and wrong-shape replies all look alike in the summary with `failed=0`.

Next: a transparent logging proxy (var/tmp-review-proxy.py, 127.0.0.1:11099 -> 127.0.0.1:11001) captures the exact request body and raw response for one genuine case with `--dry-run` (var/tmp-proxy-review-sol-20261003.log) so request-shape defects can be separated from model non-compliance before any advice is trusted.

comments.author: Lewis
comments.text:
Correction and root cause (same day): the 25/5/1 "unanswered" tallies are not model replies.

With BOTH lanes routed through transparent logging proxies (11098 -> NInfer 11000, 11099 -> llama.cpp 11001), `review --family athlete-identity --limit 1 --dry-run --max-tokens 8192` reported requested=1 answered=0 ... unanswered=1 ... failed=0 after 89.56 s, and both proxy logs stayed empty: no HTTP request was ever sent.

Cause: packets.rs::SubjectIndex::packet for AthleteIdentity calls compare_members, which requires the subject and the other member to be in one duplicate group of AthleteIndex keyed by the canonical triple (school, normalized canonical_name, grad_year) (athlete_flags.rs::key). The cases themselves were filed by athlete_clusters.rs::bound_case from the observation-level AthleteIdentityIndex (census-domain identity_index.rs), whose keys are provider-object/person evidence. A case bound by a shared provider object whose sides differ in school or grad-year attribution therefore has no group in the packet index; ask_lanes sends nothing, records.rs::account counts the case unanswered while failed=0 (no transport error happened), and review_checkpoint.rs::needs_advice charges budget for phantom asks because it never consults packet availability.

The reasoning-model behaviour reported earlier is real (qwen3.8-27b-uncensored: empty `content` with finish_reason=length at <=24 tokens with populated reasoning_content; content="pong" at 3072) but it is not the cause of these tallies since no request was sent at all.

Filed as athletic-rust-pipeline-qw2 (P1) with the full evidence and a fix direction.

title: Release gate vet lane is red: supply-chain config replaced and imports.lock stale
description: tools/gate.sh lane_vet runs 'cargo vet --locked', which fails on main with: 'ERROR Your cargo-vet store (supply-chain) has consistency errors: imports.lock is out-of-date with respect to configuration'. Commit 8b34110d ('Fix GradYear import and compilation errors across workspace') replaced the 1386-line supply-chain/config.toml (all crate exemptions plus 'audit-as-crates-io' policies) with an 11-line stub whose Google import points at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/rust-crate-audits/main/audits.toml instead of google/supply-chain, and imports.lock was not regenerated, so cargo vet refuses to run under --locked. title: restate_kill_restart::a_killed_endpoint_resumes_its_run_and_repeats_no_durable_write fails under load
description:
## Description
Observed 2026-10-01: the test failed at 122.5 s in 'cargo nextest run -p census-service' (520 passed, 1 failed) while the release gate ran concurrently; it passed at 126.4 s earlier the same day in a full-workspace run. Related: athletic-rust-pipeline-rtv (the recovery kill ladder, fixed in 4de36fc1).

## Steps to Reproduce
Run the documented focused native killed-endpoint test with full output and controlled competing load after integration. The prior failure is ground truth; do not rerun just to confirm it. Capture the assertion/deadline and reached boundary to diagnose the remaining defect.

## Acceptance Criteria
Identify whether the prior failure was a deadline or exact durable-effect violation; keep full diagnostic output. Fix the demonstrated cause without weakening recovery assertions. Quiet and controlled-loaded actual native runs preserve exact physical effects/receipts and original invocation; existing4t9 incidental-count removal is retained.
acceptance_criteria: Full diagnostic and evidence-backed root cause; exact reached native recovery passes quiet and controlled-load runs without weakened assertions; no claim that a timeout implies data loss or vice versa.
close_reason: Root cause: deadline/outer-cap under host contention, not a durable-effect violation. Focused a_killed_endpoint test passes quiet (7.984 s in-test) and with 'cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features' running concurrently (8.113 s; that lane 2522/2522 in 36.988 s), both showing the full sequence (caller cancelled at kill, repeat refused as existing invocation, paused invocation resumed). Test budgets are 60 s ready / 300 s run, so the recorded 122.5 s and 85.6 s failures were the invoking wrapper's 180 s cap on a saturated host; no durable-effect assertion (observations == expected, snapshot row counts) was ever reached and failed. The one load-sensitive code path that could abort early, paused_invocation returning on the first non-success admin response, is fixed in cc23986c and verified by docs/VERIFICATION-EVIDENCE.md 'School-site crawl lane implemented and accepted'.

title: Per-field source provenance in directory collapse
description: Black-hat review (2026-09-30) finding 2: SchoolDirectoryEntry::absorb computes one priority per record (Priority::strongest(&sources)) and applies it to every field, so a field contributed by a weaker source inherits the record's stronger rank. Counterexample: a CCD row with no phone absorbs a state-agency phone; a later CCD row with a different phone now ties on priority and the winner is decided by value order instead of CCD precedence. ADR-020 section 7 promises field union by source priority. Fix: track per-field provenance (Field -> SourceLabel, serde-default so stored rows stay readable), merge each field by its own provenance, and carry the winning source when a field is taken. Acceptance: the counterexample keeps the CCD phone; persist/read round-trip unchanged for rows written before the change.

Severity: P2

Function: SheetWriter::start; write_workbook
Impact: The performance spill/partition pipeline does not bound workbook-cell memory: every row from every completed worksheet remains in the standard-memory workbook until all sheets have rendered and save runs. Large national output therefore still grows with total represented cells.
Evidence: Cargo.toml:21 enables the constant_memory feature, but SheetWriter::start uses book.add_worksheet. Pinned rust_xlsxwriter 0.99.1 workbook.rs:514-523 constructs Worksheet::new, whose worksheet.rs:1884 sets use_constant_memory=false. worksheet.rs:15863-15865 explicitly stores all cells in standard mode. Only add_worksheet_with_constant_memory sets inline strings and use_constant_memory=true (workbook.rs:592-593). write_workbook:151-154 saves after all objective sheets are rendered.
Counterexample: Write 1,000,001 valid, small performance rows. Output partitions into two sheets and temporary projection rows can be dropped, but the normal writer retains the first sheet's populated cells while writing the second. Increasing the number of performance partitions increases simultaneously retained cell maps; no giant school or string is needed. The 20-million-observation store cap permits much larger finite inputs.
Caller defenses: A feature flag compiles the optional API; it does not activate the memory mode. The existing spill target and Excel row bounds do not change the worksheet insert_cell branch. No runtime RSS/throughput/OOM value is asserted, and the full input dataset remains a separate known memory obligation.
Required repair: Select a supported bounded-memory worksheet mode for sequential writers after auditing its restrictions (row ordering, formatting/filter behavior and writer error propagation). Combine it with byte-bounded derivation/spill, not a flag-only change, and prove full-cell readback remains equal.
Regression test: Add a multiple-performance-partition artifact regression plus representative exporter allocation/RSS measurements with exact record equality. Show live worksheet-cell retention does not scale with completed rows/partitions and preserve all source IDs, cells, formats and filters. No benchmark was run in this review.

Impact: After source acquisition advances, repeating a normal report/bests/consolidate request can return the prior completed result and old output without reading the new store. There is no caller-exposed export generation selector for these commands.

The defect is the absence of a way for these current-data commands to identify a newly requested generation, and presentation still says "wrote". Function: RangeFiles::range_of; ranges_for; read_range
Impact: The nominal 250,000-row spill target does not bound peak per-range memory. Skewed valid school populations or common/blank school display names can re-materialize the complete performance projection in one Vec before writing partitions.
Evidence: ranges_for only chooses ceil(total / RANGE_ROWS) capped by school-name count/MAX_RANGES. range_of maps every row with the same school name to the same range. read_range:229-247 pushes every parsed row into Vec and sorts, with no range byte/row budget or fallible reservation. Store table cap is 20,000,000 observations, not a per-school/athlete performance cap; frozen-input 8 GiB is a later serialized-file cap.
Counterexample: Provide 500,001 small valid performances whose historical result teams all map to one school display name. ranges_for requests three ranges then caps to the name universe, but all 500,001 rows share one rank and therefore one range. That range necessarily exceeds 250,000. More schools with all performances concentrated at one name have the same escape; no giant record is needed.
Caller defenses: Partitioning output at 1,000,000 data rows limits Excel row counts, not the input sort range. The global 20-million-row and 8-GiB file limits constrain total accepted scale but do not establish the claimed per-stage RAM/work bounds. No measured RSS, time or OOM is asserted in this review.
Required repair: Use byte-bounded sorted runs independent of school skew, followed by a bounded k-way merge in display order, or an equivalent proven bounded ordering mechanism. Bound spill file/record bytes and fallible growth; keep exact row/provenance retention.
Regression test: Add a skewed 500,001-row/same-name test and a multi-school shared-display-name case, instrument maximum live sorted-run rows/bytes, and assert configured limits with exact output multiset/order. Run representative export/RSS benchmarks only in the authorized verification lane.

Function: SchoolIndex::from_schools
Impact: A source result labeled with a shared alias is bound to whichever SchoolId entered the index first. Reversing the canonical school input changes the result affiliation without changing the source row. Incorrect school/team provenance and associated recruiting context can propagate to an athlete and performance.
Evidence: - school_index.rs:49–55 stores normalized names and aliases with or_insert_with, retaining the first ID and discarding evidence of another owner.
- school_index.rs:74–75 immediately returns that exact entry; partial():105 onward instead returns None on distinct-ID ties.
- census-crawl/wiaa/map.rs:152–158 legitimately emits school.aliases = '<city> WI'; coach_contacts/entities.rs:59–61 also emits city/state aliases, so shared aliases are produced by the current code rather than requiring corrupt records.
- Retained public capture directory_letter_a.html:87–114 publishes Abundant Life Christian (orgID 2), High School, city Madison; retained WIAA Madison East orgID 219 capture:642–643 publishes city Madison. Mapping these two captured schools through school_from_page yields the same Madison WI alias; the shared-label input is therefore supported by actual published city facts and the real emission rule, not invented aliases.
- wiaa_results/run.rs:84–86 builds SchoolIndex from canonical schools; map_rows.rs:64–71 treats resolve() as a settled SchoolId and creates the result’s team/member affiliation.
- census-service/restate_services/meets_arms/walks.rs:107–125 invokes census_crawl::wiaa_results::collect; meets_arms.rs registers wiaa_results. AthleticNet map::school_for at 79–82 also trusts this index.
Counterexample: Use the two supported WIAA school records: Abundant Life Christian (orgID 2, Madison; directory_letter_a.html:87–114) and Madison East (orgID 219, city Madison; retained WIAA school capture:642–643). They have different canonical IDs. The current WIAA school mapper emits the alias Madison WI for both. SchoolIndex::from_schools([AbundantLife, MadisonEast]).resolve(Wisconsin, Madison WI) returns AbundantLife/Exact; reversing the two records returns MadisonEast/Exact. A valid parsed result label choosing this admitted alias is bound to the selected school instead of unresolved ambiguity. No authentic captured result occurrence of the ambiguous label is claimed.
Caller defenses: Distinct school IDs and known jurisdictions do not remove the shared-label ambiguity. The partial matcher has a unique-owner check, but exact aliases bypass it. This is separate from contacts ownership’s same-name canonical-ID collision and directory campus-stripping findings. No claim is made that an authentic current result row already uses this ambiguous alias.
Required repair: Index an exact label as Unique(SchoolId) or Ambiguous owner set instead of first-wins. Return an explicit ambiguous/unresolved result for multiple distinct IDs, or require exact provider-owned school corroboration. Canonical exact names may have an explicit priority over aliases only when that priority cannot resolve a genuine owner collision by arrival order.
Regression test: Construct two real CanonicalSchool values with different IDs and a shared city alias, build both input orders, and require the same unresolved result. Exercise WIAA result mapping to ensure no team/performance is minted for that ambiguous label. Keep one-owner repeated-alias and genuinely unique partial-match controls.

Required repair: Use checked bounded file reads plus explicit capture/manifest/row/string byte and work budgets, with fallible reservation and typed resource-limit errors. Preserve valid partial interpretations and owed input when a work budget is reached.
Regression test: Boundary-size fixtures at cap−1/cap/cap+1; oversized/changing files and huge manifests must fail before materialising unbounded buffers. Budget-resume must keep unfinished capture/row work explicit.

title: ACQ-08: Acquisition efficiency counters undercount physical traffic
description:
# ACQ-08 Acquisition efficiency counters undercount physical traffic

Severity: P2
Review source: var/review-20261006/review-inbound.md:L670-L681
Epic: athletic-rust-pipeline-hfhk

ACQ-08 Acquisition efficiency counters undercount physical traffic
Severity: P2
Location: https://github.com/lprior-repo/athletic-rust-pipeline/blob/649d2bb0a694e7d337d83a37929d511e4615b894/crates/census-crawl/src/net/execute.rs#L208-L213
Function: Fetcher::cached_outcome / FetchStats::physical_requests
Impact: The aggregate physical-request denominator can become zero after real network work, disagree with per-host totals, and inflate/erase records-per-request metrics. HTTP refusal, robots and redirect-hop traffic is also missing.
Evidence: cached_outcome increments aggregate cache_hits but never aggregate requests; per_host increments both. FetchStats::physical_requests subtracts cache_hits from requests. HTTP count_request is invoked only in browser accept_capture, not attempt_once; HTTP non-200/404 and 304 have no request increment. fetch_robots performs send with no stats and reqwest redirects are invisible to counting.
Counterexample: One physical HTTP200 gives aggregate requests=1/cache_hits=0. Replay the same key once: requests remains1/cache_hits becomes1, so physical_requests=0; per_host requests=2/cache_hits=1, so its physical_requests=1. With one physical429, even aggregate requests remains0. Robots and redirect chain increase actual traffic further.
Required repair: Count every actual dispatched HTTP/browser physical request/hop exactly once, and maintain aggregate/per-origin consistency. Model logical cache accesses separately rather than deriving physical traffic from inconsistent mixed counters.
Regression test: Real fixture accounting test: robots + redirect +200 +cache replay +refresh304 +429. Assert exact server-observed physical counts match aggregate and sum of per-origin counters, with positive efficiency denominator when network traffic occurred.
Confidence: high
Evidence type: Static source trace; counterexample not executed
Runtime reproduction: Not executed for this counterexample; static source analysis.

title: ACQ-07: Non-404 HTTP refusals discard the response capture
description:
# ACQ-07 Non-404 HTTP refusals discard the response capture

Severity: P2
Review source: var/review-20261006/review-inbound.md:L658-L669
Epic: athletic-rust-pipeline-hfhk

ACQ-07 Non-404 HTTP refusals discard the response capture
Severity: P2
Location: https://github.com/lprior-repo/athletic-rust-pipeline/blob/649d2bb0a694e7d337d83a37929d511e4615b894/crates/census-crawl/src/net/execute/attempt.rs#L50-L55
Function: Fetcher::attempt_once
Impact: 403, 429 and 5xx responses have no retained immutable body/headers/digest evidence. Operators cannot inspect the actual refusal/challenge source response, and the failure-retention contract is unmet.
Evidence: Only 200 and 404 call cache_and_record/write_archive. The default arm calls status_error, which retains only status and URL. The reqwest::Response is then dropped. Browser challenge/refusal paths likewise discard BrowserCapture without write_archive (execute/browser/refusal.rs:6–40; browser.rs:89–112).
Counterexample: A public server returns 429 with a diagnostic JSON body and Retry-After:120. fetch() records an access condition and returns Http429, but archive/bodies and capture manifests receive none of the response. A 200 browser human-verification page is also dropped by refuse_challenge.
Required repair: Archive bounded failure/challenge captures before recording/refusing them, without replacing successful cache entries. Retain response status, original/final URL, relevant headers, actual fetch time and body digest; keep error dispatch separate from success caching.
Regression test: Fixture responses 403/429/500 and browser challenge200/429 must retain byte-identical immutable captures while leaving any previous successful cache entry unchanged. Test partial body failure as a typed incomplete capture where supported.
Confidence: high
Evidence type: Static source trace; counterexample not executed

title: ACQ-05: Browser GET bridge silently drops caller representation and provider headers
description:
# ACQ-05 Browser GET bridge silently drops caller representation and provider headers

Severity: P2
Review source: var/review-20261006/review-inbound.md:L634-L645
Epic: athletic-rust-pipeline-hfhk

ACQ-05 Browser GET bridge silently drops caller representation and provider headers
Severity: P2
Location: https://github.com/lprior-repo/athletic-rust-pipeline/blob/649d2bb0a694e7d337d83a37929d511e4615b894/crates/census-crawl/src/net/execute/browser.rs#L30-L34
Function: Fetcher::fetch_browser
Impact: Browser-only providers receive a different request than their adapters request. In particular, Athletic.net whole-meet acquisition supplies anettokens but the bridge cannot carry them, leading to refusals or different responses on token-dependent endpoints.
Evidence: FetchPlan carries options.headers, but RequestSpec construction forwards only URL and Action::Fetch{body:None}. bridge/wire.rs:5–19 and athleticnet-browser/request/action.rs:24–29 have no headers field. The browser JS only sets content-type for POST bodies (transport/script.rs:15–19). athleticnet/meet/collect/walk.rs:130–140 adds Accept plus the token returned by MeetData.
Counterexample: The meet endpoint returns token T. The next all-results request has FetchOptions.headers=[Accept:application/json,anettokens:T]. Because www.athletic.net is registered Browser, fetch_browser constructs a spec with neither header; a server requiring anettokens returns 403. This is source-path static evidence, not a claim that a current live endpoint was tested.
Required repair: Carry an explicitly bounded allowlisted set of adapter-request headers through browser RequestSpec and apply them to the browser fetch. Do not carry credentials or challenge-cookie bypass headers. If a header is prohibited, reject it explicitly rather than silently changing request semantics.
Regression test: Bridge roundtrip and controlled browser endpoint test requiring a benign provider header. Assert exact delivery or explicit refusal, and cover Accept content negotiation plus the whole-meet token-dependent request.
Confidence: high
Evidence type: Static source trace; counterexample not executed
Runtime reproduction: Not executed for this counterexample; static source analysis.

title: ACQ-06: Cache identity ignores representation context and accepts mismatched request metadata
description:
# ACQ-06 Cache identity ignores representation context and accepts mismatched request metadata

Severity: P2
Review source: var/review-20261006/review-inbound.md:L646-L657
Epic: athletic-rust-pipeline-hfhk

ACQ-06 Cache identity ignores representation context and accepts mismatched request metadata
Severity: P2
Location: https://github.com/lprior-repo/athletic-rust-pipeline/blob/649d2bb0a694e7d337d83a37929d511e4615b894/crates/census-crawl/src/net/cache.rs#L41-L48
Function: Fetcher::key_for / read_cache / cached_outcome
Impact: Two semantically different representations of a URL reuse one success. An internally valid pair copied to the wrong cache key can be relabelled as the requested URL/method instead of being rejected, despite correct body SHA256 checks.
Evidence: key_for hashes method, raw URL and body string only; execute.rs:142–147 supplies no options.headers or source/representation context. CacheMeta has no request-header/body identity. read_cache:121–134 validates status/size/digest but not URL/method against the requested key; cached_outcome execute.rs:215–218 replaces those values with caller URL/method.
Counterexample: GET the same valid public URL first with Accept:text/html and then with Accept:application/json, refresh=false. A content-negotiating response cached from the first call is returned to the JSON caller without a physical request. For integrity, place a valid URL-B 200 body/meta pair under URL-A key: read_cache succeeds and cached_outcome returns URL-A with B's bytes.
Required repair: Construct a canonical bounded request/representation identity including relevant normalised headers and body media type, retain it in capture metadata, and validate metadata against the requested identity before cache replay. Keep source-independent immutable byte dedup separate from request identity.
Regression test: Controlled Vary:Accept fixture must produce separate captures/cache entries and independent replay. A valid pair renamed under a foreign method/URL key must be quarantined/refused rather than accepted. Verify case/order canonicalisation of equivalent headers.
Confidence: high
Evidence type: Static source trace; counterexample not executed
Runtime reproduction: Not executed for this counterexample; static source analysis.

title: [bug] An accepted different_person verdict does not resolve its case: index returns it to retained and writes no decision
description:
## OBSERVED (2026-10-06, store var/review-dual-gpu-20261005/store, repaired portable binary)
The dual-lane review accepted two different_person verdicts for one athlete pair:
  Athlete identity:ath_subject_23fa840c8a9683f9:p2:f3e198db1d1fb1dd  value different_person conf 90 outcome agreement
  Athlete identity:ath_subject_2d4d7c348d0aa4a4:p2:f3e198db1d1fb1dd  value different_person conf 90 outcome agreement
  both lanes 95/90 admitted; case states after the review pass 239 pending / 122 retained / 99 resolved; verdict counter 99 accepted / 14 refused.
Then 'census-service --store <S> index' reported 'index source_identities=33041 conflicts=59 reviews=270 superseded=0 coverage=56 snapshots=1' and moved:
  athlete_identity_decisions 30244 -> 30341 (+97 = exactly the 97 deterministic same_person acceptances)
  source_identities 31349 -> 31520, conflicts 61 -> 59, review case keys 460 -> 714 (consolidate exports 476 live rows)
  case states after: pending 239 / retained 140 / resolved 97
All 113 verdict-bearing case ids survive in the export, but both model-accepted different_person cases are back to 'retained' and no identity decision exists for that pair in athlete_identity_decisions.

## IMPACT
An accepted 'keep separate' decision is durable only as a verdict row: the derivation does not consume it, the pair stays a duplicate candidate (retained) after every derivation pass, so the case cannot reach resolved and the separation is invisible to the identity projection.

## ACCEPTANCE
Either an accepted different_person verdict resolves its case (and is represented in the identity projection or decision table so a later derivation does not return it to retained), or the owning document states that only same_person acceptances are applied and records why the case state may legitimately go back to retained.
notes: Review 2026-10-06 IDENTITY-03 (Every agreed DifferentPerson verdict is rejected by identity application): same defect as this bead — positive_identity at crates/census-domain/src/model/identity_corroboration.rs:68-73 returns false for accepted DifferentPerson, and census-reconcile/index/apply.rs:19-29 then persists the case as Retained with no separation decision, exactly the accepted different_person verdict 'does not resolve its case / writes no decision' defect tracked by bpe4 — see var/review-20261006/review-inbound.md:L914-L930

title: render_required mislabels rows whose fetched body already carries the claimed person
description: coachverify/evidence.rs RowEvidence::verdict reaches RenderRequired whenever no claim matched and the body contains a script tag, which reads as a rendering gap but is usually an attribution gap: the fetched bytes already hold the evidence. serialized contracts and identity acceptance; the adapter owner owns the new lane, its fixtures and

title: A/B measure the derived/evidence keyspace split before claiming it
description:
The 2026-10-06 storage review recommended benchmarking a physical split of the entities keyspace (evidence vs derived) before adopting it, on the grounds that a nationwide derived rebuild should not drive compaction/write amplification through the largely immutable evidence tree. Decision: no split without a representative measurement, consistent with ADR-001 (persistent indexes require a measured query need) and ADR-025 (the derived/evidence partition is logical; a physical split is unclaimed).

A prior attempt at this harness (agent KeyspaceBench, gpu3090-coder) failed: it reported files_changed crates/census-store/examples/keyspace_ab.rs, xtask/src/main.rs, xtask/README.md and run_command 'env -u CI tools/moon-local run pipeline:xtask -- storage-ab --evidence-rows 20000 --derived-rows 40000 --generations 2', but none of those edits exist in the arh-storage-gen worktree (verified 2026-10-06: file absent, xtask/src/main.rs and xtask/README.md unmodified) and it never executed the harness.

Required work: an offline harness that writes deterministic synthetic evidence and derived rows into (a) one entities keyspace and (b) split keyspaces, measuring the store's own derived-generation rebuild path (stage, publish, reclaim) for insert/rebuild/point-read throughput, on-disk bytes and RSS; execute it with real commands through Moon (no direct cargo); record exact commands, dataset sizes, repeated runs and observed deltas in docs/VERIFICATION-EVIDENCE.md. A split is adopted only if the measured advantage is real and stable; otherwise record the negative result and close.

title: Identity: 5898 row-scoped WIAA athletes can never reach verified status
description:
## DEFECT (design limit to record or repair)
The 5898 athletes whose only identity is a `wiaa_result_row` key can never become `verified`: `person_provider` admits only four person namespaces, so their identity facts are never `source_bound` and no `SourceBound` application can be derived, whatever their evidence.

## EXACT EVIDENCE
- `crates/census-domain/src/model/identity_decision.rs:100-106` — `person_provider` returns `Some` only for `MilesplitAthlete`, `TfrrsAthlete`, `DirectAthleticsAthlete` and `AthleticNet { kind: "athlete" }`; `:107-115` — `person_key` additionally requires a nonzero canonical decimal id.
- `crates/census-domain/src/model/identity_index.rs:77-84` — `source_bound = primary.is_some() && parsed`; with `wiaa_result_row` mapping to `None`, `primary` is `None`.
- `crates/census-domain/src/model/identity_application.rs:49-55` — a subject without `isolated_source` is retained with `CompetingSourceClaims`; `crates/census-domain/src/model/identity_projection.rs:130-137` — status then stays `Unverified`/`RetainedConflict`.
- Workbook: 5898 rows have no profile URL; all 5898 are `identity_status=unverified` and `review_status=review`; the JSON's `wiaa_result_row` namespace count is exactly 5898 (`var/verify-round2-20261006/w4/wb_identity_cross.json`, `json_store_probe.out`). 3366 of them appear in the best-results CSV, 2532 carry only Performances rows (`var/verify-round2-20261006/w4/athlete_key_coverage.json`).
- Row keys are text-derived, e.g. `https://www.wiaawi.org/sites/default/files/2026-08/tr2026chiltonsectionalindiv.pdf:4x800 Relay Division 2 <runs of spaces> Finals <runs of spaces> 1) Gentry, Jude 9:<none>:1:leg3` (raw token, `final_samples.out`).
- Report: `var/verify-round2-20261006/w4/w4-identity-caller-evidence.md` section 1.

## WORK
Decide and record one of: (a) accept that timing rows are not person documents and state the 5898 permanently-unverified rows as a coverage limit; or (b) add a qualified person namespace for WIAA athlete ids where the source publishes them, with its own evidence rule.

## LIMITS
Read-only verification on 2026-10-06; no store table (source identities, review cases) was reopened for these athletes because the delivered store is empty.

title: coach_gate cannot verify render_required rows: its fetcher is built without with_browser_lane
description: The coach_gate example builds its fetcher without with_browser_lane, so a tap row whose cached capture is a script-driven shell is reported render_required and can never be verified or shipped. In the recorded 2026-10-05 run (var/tap-integration-20261005/, var/tap-fragments-gate-20261005/) the verdicts were 1 verified, 1010 render_required, 3051 mismatch, 19566 empty, 4005 fetch-failed out of 27633 rows; the render_required share is the only class blocked purely by missing client-side rendering. Evidence: a NJ row's capture is 238063 bytes with four <script> tags and no server-rendered contact text (docs/VERIFICATION-EVIDENCE.md, 'Coach-tap wave-2 chain verified end to end'). Wrap or extend the gate's fetcher with the browser lane census-crawl already provides, then re-run the gate and confirm the render_required class drops below the shipped threshold.
close_reason: Measured false as stated. The lane cannot carry these hosts by design: ADMITTED_BROWSER_ORIGINS is [www.athletic.net] (census-crawl/src/net/bridge/mod.rs), routing is registry-driven (net/execute.rs:186 via registry::transport_for_host), and BrowserLane::answer submits to a Restate ingress object (bridge/lane.rs), so a standalone gate example has no serving BrowserSession. Rendering is also not established to help: a headless dump of the recorded render_required host www.njsiaa.org page 7 returned 0 table rows and no contact text, while the already-fetched body held 51 table rows including the shipped contact. And 704 of 720 render_required rows with a cached body already contained both the school name and the claimed person (203 with a role word within 160 chars and the school within 3000). The real defect is the verdict label/matcher, filed separately; evidence: var/tap-wave2-20261005/render-probe/ (measurement.txt, measure-render-required.py, njsiaa-page7-headless-dump.html).

title: [bug] claims_for_row compares state exactly, so a lowercase state cell drops a kept row's claims
description: census_service::coachverify::claims_for_row selects a row's claims with claim.state == row.state. write_state_union files a row under the uppercased state (report.rs) and merge_coaches::load::from_fields uppercases the row's state, but a fragment whose state cell is lowercase produces claims carrying the original case, so read_fragment_evidence selects nothing for that row and reconcile fails closed ('proof digest mismatch' or an unmatched row) instead of reconciling it. All 27633 rows of the 2026-10-05 tap fragments carry uppercase two-letter state cells, so the acceptance run is unaffected; the comparison should be case-insensitive (or both sides normalized) before this lane takes foreign input. Observed 2026-10-05 while landing the coach-tap integration (var/tap-integration-20261005/).
close_reason: Fixed in cli/merge_coaches/load.rs and pinned by a regression. Root cause: load_rows/Row::from_fields uppercased the row's state cell, so a lowercase-state union row was published with state 'OH' while its claims kept the verbatim 'oh'; the digest validator (census-domain/model/contact_proof/validation.rs, validate_claim_against_row) compares state/role/school/value/person exactly, so the row's proof could never reconcile and the selector's exact compare only surfaced it as a missing sidecar. The selector's exact compare is correct as the mirror of that domain rule - making it case-insensitive alone would still be rejected by validate_claim_against_row. Fix: preserve the state cell verbatim (trim only) in both from_fields and load_rows, and normalize only dedupe_key's state so 'oh'/'OH' still dedupe. Regression merge_keeps_a_state_cells_case_so_the_proof_still_validates failed before the fix (CheckFailure: the merge publishes the state cell as the union wrote it; left="OH" right="oh") and passes after; focused lane 59/59, pipeline:gate PASS 2533/2533; the recorded all-uppercase NJ tap data re-ran byte-identical (merge rows, sidecars and the whole reconcile-out tree) with the rebuilt binary census-service d3eaa867. Evidence: docs/VERIFICATION-EVIDENCE.md entry 'Coach-tap wave-2 chain verified end to end', var/tap-wave2-20261005/verify5.log.
